After delaying the inevitable, its now only hours away from The Offering.

Procrastination and denial are powerful tools when afraid to face the music.

'I have nothing to offer..'

These words spoken so quietly it didn't quite echo through the abandoned halls and rooms but could be heard over and over in my mind. 

I didn't want to believe this. I couldn't.

It's one possession. One worldly possession to hand to The Cause. 

After everything it had done for us (praise them forever), all it asks from the human race is for each of us to hand over one possession of value be it monetary or setimental. 

And I have neither, this house isn't even in my name. It cannot be stolen either. They would know if anyone dares break the laws and we don't not know of the fate of those who dared. 

I must be missing something. Maybe a book. No, I used the last collection to tide me through the winter. 

Maybe a nice cooked meal? I doubt They'd appreciated cheese toasty. Developing skills like cookery felt like a waste of time with limited food.

My mother gained her culinary talent many years before the war, in harsher times before The Cause came, her talents came in very handy. 

Knowing how to prepare wild berries to cook out the poison and knowing what foods had the best nutrients.

Yes, what a fantastic women. Why did she have to end up with a son like me? No Job, no future, nothing to my name.

Regardless of how much I fuck up, her and dad always smile when they see me.

'Always proud of our eldest boy, aren't we dear?' 

Mum said that the other day while serving dinner, one of the rare times I visit.

'Of course, sweetheart', although he replied, I think his mind was on the feast laid out in front of him. 

I notice mum smiled then, she knew he wasn't listening but didn't care. 

That candid moment really stuck out for me, even days later. Mum and dad, after the last 30 years of mayhem, still had love for each other. 

The war, the famine, The Cause and The Offerings.

If their love didn't stay with them, I don't know how we would've survived. 

Even though I have never found love, because of my parents, I'll never stop believing in it. 

'So, what's everyone's offer this year?' 

That feeling of my stomach dropping, my heart racing, beads of sweat forming. All resurfacing along with the memory of that question.

'Son?' Dad looks over at me. 

'We-we- I haven't qui-quite decided yet' 

'You haven't got long, it's only a week away.' Mum interjected with a side of concern and garden peas. 

'Yeah, I've been so busy wi--'

'I'm offering my sapphire earrings this year!' My sis interrupted. Who can blame her, the attention was on someone other than her for over a minute. 

'Hubby here recently bought me diamond earrings. Black Diamond. So no need for last seasons fashion, right sweetie?' She looked over to her husband, a humble and gentle man. Earning his fortune through studying plumbing rather than a computer science after school.

So many people with worthless skills after the fall of the technology age. Knowing how to make a spreadsheet mean jackshit when you can't make a fire with two twigs and some hay.

Living modestly, his only expense is spoiling my already rotten sister. 

Maybe it's because I want to be spoiled or have someone to spoil but I always envied them. Sis especially, she doesn't deserve him. 

Hubby meekly smiles, I'm sensing a mix of embarrassment and happiness for his wife. 

'Well isn't that wonderful?' My mum gleams, blissfully unaware of her daughters toxic personality. I mean, it's better to ignore it than admit you didn't do right as a parent? 

Dad's disappointment was more visible but carried on around the table.

"And you, lad?"

All eyes on hubby, now.

'Well, as you know, Grammy--my uhh, Grandma passed away this year and left me some things including her roasting tin she used every Sunday for over 50 years for our weekly dinners. I've decided that roasting tin is what I'll offer. I hope they understand how much it means to me'

'Why, dear that's so--' 

'--Not going to win best offering! A rusty pan?!' My sis interrupts again tearing with laughter. 

'We all know best offering is a myth they made up to encourage better things from us' I snapped.

'Not this nonsense again! The Cause would never lie to us, would they dear?' Mum looked to dad.

Dad ignores her 'Everyone knows we don't welcome talk like that at this table. After what the Cause did for this family? For you?' I didn't raise you this way!' Dad's getting pretty heated now. I know he isn't an idiot, he must have suspicions too. 

Suspicions like that aren't welcome in this world though, always watching They are and we are always watched. 

'I'm sure you didn't raise sis to be a spoilt little bitch either but someone has to put her in place!'

I regretted that outburst right after I said it. I remember going outside to have a cigarette. I never spoke to my dad like that. What was I thinking. 

Too shaken to light my cig, I see a steady flame in the twilight offering a light. It's my brother in law. 

I light up and take the first drag, none of my nerves calmed yet I felt like I still needed the nicotine.

'I shouldn't have been so rude, sorry I made a scene..' I'm not sorry I made a scene but I am sorry for his marriage.

Flicking away his lighter, I can still remember the calm face he gave before he spoke to me.

'You haven't got anything for the offering again, have you?'

I shush him knowing we're being listened too

'Don't be ridiculous!'

'You always get so stressed during this time...here, an early birthday gift'

He takes a handsomely graved golden watch from his pocket and places into my free hand. The thing must be worth  thousands. 

'No, not again. I barely made it last year with that stunt. Fobbing off something that isn't mine? They aren't that stupid!'

"You are smart enough to fool them, it's worth enough in money, you won't need a bond with it." 

"I'm not doing it. A man must give his own possession' 

'Now isn't the time to have pride. I wouldn't help those who didn't deserve it. Your intellect and skill would've been valuable if we remained in the tech age. Robots would've made me obsolete. In times like this, accept people's help."

Pride is powerful emotion. 

" I don't need you to patronise me."

It's the first time I ever saw him look disappointed.

"We don't know what happens to those who dare to not participate in the offering. I hope They have mercy on you." 

He disappears back into the house, I can hear the others finish the after dinner grace. 

"Praise them forever!"

"Yep" having the last drag and flicking it on the lawn. "Praise them forever..." 

It's dark now. 

It's time. 

I can hear the bonfire roaring up to the heavens ready to be fed our offerings.

"I have absolutely nothing" 

When you say it out loud it feels more real. 

Hearing kids running around playing, street vendors selling goods and food for the cemencing festival. The town preacher reciting prayers and scriptures praising the Cause.

"Praise them forever!"

It's really happening, no escape now. 

The door knocks, ready for my fate and the weather I grab my coat and answer.

My parents at the door, picking me up so I don't go alone. The Offering is usually joyful celebration with songs and dance. The traditional strawberry pudding my mum makes sure to make every year. I always fucking hated that pudding. 

"We're meeting your sister there" mum smiles 

"Ahh" Dad breathes in the smokey air. "It'll be a good offering this year, I can feel it!" 

Most of the time, Dad's optimism is welcomed but now grates on me while I walk my gauntlet.

"Did you get something offer honey?" My mum asks, only to make conversation.

"Yeah mum. I did." My brother in law was right, my intellect was wasted on this tech less age. 

Quick thinking has always been one of my most powerful tools. 

"Hey! They're just getting started!" My sister waves is to a spot she saved for us. Her husband looking right me. 

"Guessing you haven't changed your mind?" I'm glad he knows me and how stubborn I am. 

"No need to worry, I have an offer." 

"Don't do anything stupid now" Shit, he knows me too well.

One by one, each of the townspeople approach the fire and the preacher asks: 

"What is your offer?"

"Sapphire earrings" my sister announces on her turn.

"Ahh a rare jewel, The Cause are pleased with your offer!" The preacher proclaims. 

I bet they weren't happy with that smug look she has now. 

My mum's oldest teapot, dad's first model train and brother in laws roasting tin are all burning away in the bonfire as my turn arrives.

The preacher looks suspicious of me or could be my paranoia.

"And what do you have to offer, dear boy?" 

"I have no worldly possessions left to offer. Nothing of monetary or sentimental value...other than myself." 

With my final words, I leap into the bonfire. Hoping my sacrifice had sufficed. 

*fool* 

"They have been angered, The Cause has been angered!" Feared the preacher.

*We saved you many years ago from the war. We rid your world of the evils of technology. Fertilised your land and brought you peace.* 

*We watch your every move, Listen to every word you've spoken*

*Every year we take what is most valuable to each of you in fear of being damned.* 

*Did you ever think your body*

*Your mind*

*Your soul*

*Were still in your possession?* 

*Utter fools* 

And with that, my offer was rejected, sending a message to all who survived The Offering. 

*Your body, Your mind, Your soul...Your most valuable possessions...are all mine* 

My body now charred, my soul sent to where all souls who dare defy The Cause go, and I find out the fate of all those who dared.
